root_cause: The outlet decided whether a popped route had finished from the controller status of the previous frame: RouteOutlet::drive_route_animations runs before the frame, and the runtime ticks controllers inside run_frame after the outlet has composed. A reverse that ended on frame N was dismissed during frame N but was only removed on frame N+1. Flutter ticks before the build, so dismissal runs finalizeRoute and removes the route on frame N.
change: crates/incular-runtime/src/route_outlet.rs: retain_unfinished_exits takes the frame time and treats a run that is done at `now` as finished. This covers popped routes and the replacement a replaced route waits for. Popped controllers that leave this way are ticked at `now` after the bookkeeping borrow is released, so status listeners hear Dismissed on that frame. crates/incular-animation/src/controller.rs (outside ownership, additive): AnimationController::is_done_at(now), a pure query that does not tick. A pre-tick of all controllers was tried and dropped: it desyncs OpacityController, whose tick only updates its opacity when the inner controller tick changes.
tests: crates/incular-runtime/tests/runtime/route_outlet.rs::popped_fade_and_default_page_routes_stay_mounted_through_reverse (now asserts removal on the frame the reverse ends)
harness: navigation__navigator__fade_pop_timeline and navigation__hero__pop_flight_navigator: the probe.top.present / hero_to.present divergence at frame 44 is gone. Remaining fields are outside this finding: the top opacity residual of about 0.005 (harness start instant), below.opacity (secondary animation, Flutter 0.973 at frame 4), hero flight geometry (harness request) and covered root opacity.
limitations: crates/incular/tests/heroes.rs::heroes_do_not_fly_without_a_route_animation_or_on_pop still fails at line 391. This failure is known from before (residual pass), the test-alignment worker owns that test, and the test does not use RouteOutlet. A push that completes does not yet occlude the route below on the same frame (transition_settled still reads last-frame status); no scenario shows that.
note: Confirmed before fixing: frame 44 diverged on both scenarios.

root_cause: ModalRoute::of reads an inherited value that the outlet installs with Widget::environment_scope. That scope is a non-constraint-dependent LayoutBuilder whose child is built during layout. WidgetTree::validate_widget_subtree (incular-widgets/src/tree/reconciliation.rs:2042) stops at builder nodes, so route content under the scope is only validated during layout (InvalidGeneratedChild) after the outlet rebuild has applied. That breaks the atomic DuplicateKey contract (route_outlet.rs::outlet_rebuild_failure_consumes_nothing and the other duplicate-key tests).
limitations: Remaining work, all in incular-widgets tree internals (outside this group and heavily shared): (1) give environment_scope / shared_environment_scope a statically known child, for example a WidgetKind::LayoutBuilder field static_child: Option<Widget>, and have validate_widget_subtree descend into it; (2) while descending below a scope, take the ambient TextDirection from the scope value when it is a TextDirection, and otherwise skip MissingDirectionality checks under scopes, so Directionality-style scopes do not falsely fail; (3) optionally build such static scopes eagerly during reconciliation. After that, flip RouteOutlet::new to modal_route_scopes: true and keep the duplicate-key tests unchanged. No outlet-only design gives eager validation: the outlet has no access to tree validation, and any wrapper that publishes a value is a lazy scope.
note: Rust-first alternative considered: publishing the route through element identity (route tag lookup) instead of an inherited value. BuildContext has no ancestor-key query, so this would also need a widgets API.

root_cause: Route::overlay entries had no host anywhere: the outlet rejected them typed (UnsupportedPresentation), and nothing else read RoutePresentation::Overlay. Flutter's OverlayRoute inserts its entries into the navigator's own overlay.
change: crates/incular-runtime/src/route_outlet.rs: new host_overlay_routes policy (default true; set_host_overlay_routes / host_overlay_routes). compose mounts hosted overlay routes at their stack position. route_body composes the entries in order, puts a veil before each entry with a barrier (blocks input, dismisses the route) and wraps everything in the route transition and heroes through the new Route::present. The route's tagged wrapper blocks semantics of earlier routes when an entry has a barrier. Exiting overlay routes use the same body. preflight rejects only when hosting is disabled. crates/incular-navigation/src/presentation.rs: Route::present(content) (presented_child now delegates to it). Docs for OutletPlacement, ExternalOverlay and UnsupportedPresentation are updated.
tests: Seven rejection/atomicity tests opt out with set_host_overlay_routes(false) and are otherwise unchanged: outlet_rejects_overlay_routes_explicitly, outlet_failed_attempt_output_and_followup_agree, nested_unsupported_rejected_with_outlet_identity, nested_valid_siblings_present_and_recover_independently, outlet_unsupported_introduced_mid_build_fails_explicitly, outlet_rejected_configuration_schedules_no_retry, outlet_preflight_failure_preserves_attempt_state
api_change: Behavior change: overlay routes now mount in RouteOutlet by default instead of failing the frame. Migration: an application that hosts those entries in its own OverlayPortal calls outlet.set_host_overlay_routes(false) to keep the typed rejection. Additive: RouteOutlet::set_host_overlay_routes, RouteOutlet::host_overlay_routes, Route::present.
limitations: The transition wraps all of a route's entries, barrier veils included: a fade fades the barrier too, which is close to ModalRoute, but a slide also slides the barrier. Entries are never opaque and are unmounted while covered by an opaque page (Flutter OverlayEntry defaults); there is no per-entry opaque or maintainState flag. The route's own child is not shown for overlay routes. Flutter's ModalRoute barrier plus content was already provided by the Modal and Popup presentations.

root_cause: Two dispatcher types exist. The app-shell RootBackButtonDispatcher (incular-widgets/src/app_shell/router.rs:635-746) is the only type RouterConfig::with_back_button_dispatcher accepts (:866), and it is a flat newest-first callback list. The navigation BackButtonDispatcher (incular-widgets/src/navigation/back_dispatch.rs:413-428) already has create_child and defer_to, but the Router cannot use it.
harness: not applicable (no Router back-event twin; harness request 3)
limitations: Remaining work: make RouterConfig accept the navigation BackButtonDispatcher, or a trait both types implement. Add ChildBackButtonDispatcher semantics to it: take_priority (the parent forwards to this child first), forget, and parent fallback when every child declines. Have a nested Router built with a child dispatcher call take_priority when it becomes active. Then retire or adapt RootBackButtonDispatcher, which is a public API change across app_shell/router.rs and the window back-event plumbing. This was not attempted because the time went to items 1-3.

root_cause: There is no declarative page-diff hook. Navigator page-list updates apply additions and removals directly, and the outlet animates any newly seen route in and any popped top route out. There is no per-route decision record (Flutter RouteTransitionRecord markForPush/markForAdd/markForPop/markForComplete/markForRemove).
limitations: Remaining work (Rust-first): a TransitionDelegate trait on Navigator that receives the diff as typed lists (new top pages, kept pages and removed pages with their positions) and returns a decision per route: Push/Add for entering pages and Pop/Complete/Remove for leaving pages. Provide a DefaultTransitionDelegate: only the new top animates in (push), other added pages are added without animation, the old top animates out (pop), other removed pages are removed at once. The outlet's drive_route_animations already has the needed mechanics (forward_on_next_tick vs set_value(1.0), and exiting routes vs immediate removal), so the delegate decisions would be stored per route by the navigator and consumed there instead of the current newly-seen/previous-top heuristics.
note: Deferred for API size; the outlet mechanics now handle same-frame removal, so the remaining work is the delegate API and navigator bookkeeping.
